system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
system.sibling_key: COME RETRIBUTION fits March–April passages; COMPLETE VICTORY encrypts the two 9 March orders introducing that key; THE NAVY OUR PRIDE is recovered from 9 January external plaintext. Key use varies by recipient.
system.notes: Distinct symbols: the 26-letter alphabet of the tabula recta. The clerks' capitals mislead in a few recurring ways (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, a U-like glyph for IC); every correction is a single glyph and is listed in alignment.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.

solution.what: Fetched the NARA catalogue records of vols. 196, 11 and 10 and the full-resolution frames listed in the catalogue's OCR run lists; screened them on montages. Vol. 196 frame 0027 has no cipher words (an OCR false hit).
Read the cipher words of vol. 196 fr. 0061 (180 letters) and vol. 11 frs. 0022, 0036 and 0039 (52, 56 and 61 letters) and the clear text around them from the images.

Applied the known Confederate key COMERETRIBUTION, over the cipher letters only, offset 0 at each telegram: English from the first letter in all four telegrams (171/180, 50/52, 46/57, 59/61 letters right as read).

Explained the remaining letters as single misleading glyphs of the clerks' capitals (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, U-like glyph for IC); no correction needs more than one glyph.

Controls on the letters as read (decrypt.py --controls): COMERETRIBUTION offset 0 chi2 19-37; best other offset 92-676; COMPLETEVICTORY 132-381; MANCHESTERBLUFF 133-1072; 200 random keys minimum 75-402; shuffled cipher words with the right key 3-10 letters agreeing on average.

OCR full text of OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 searched for each plaintext phrase: the 6 April telegram to Levy is printed in clear on p. 1209. The 12 and 30 March and 8 April telegrams not found in this first search.

Second, independent agent: re-read all four telegrams on its own crops, decrypted them with its own code (same plaintext, 171/180, 50/52, 59/61 letters right as read), corrected the 12 March letter count to 180, read the 8 April date line, and found that the 8 April telegram is printed in clear in OR I/49/2 p. 1216 (the first search missed it because of double spaces in the OCR text). Searched OR I/49 pt. 1 for the 12 March telegram: not found.
The four telegrams written as sentences (<doc>_reading.md). One hole: [?west] in the 12 March telegram, where the cipher gives WEST and the sense wants 'what'.
Located three additional telegrams in OR I/45/2 p.772 and I/49/2 pp.1223,1255; no complete counterpart verified for 18 January. Search failures and limits in WORKLOG.md.
Matched 9 January ciphertext against OR plaintext to infer THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; 86/94 candidate letters agree. Retrospective partition check is not an independent blind holdout.
Transcribed six continuation telegrams; all candidate glyphs remain distinct from reconstructed cipher letters. Retained partial 18 January and unresolved April passages.

Verified two orders dated 9 March to Wirt Adams and D.W. Adams introducing COME RETRIBUTION after this date under COMPLETE VICTORY; 46/47 candidate letters each agree. Wirt copy has complete pencilled decipherment, date/hand unknown.
Replayed alignments; tested alternative known keys/all offsets, 1000 random keys for 9 January, and arithmetic round-trip. No ciphertext-only solver or independent holdout claim.
Added five externally/adjacently supported full readings and one provisional 18 January reading. Partial 8 March Brent fragments support earlier key use in another channel; no full transcript claim.
Refreshed community status: PR186 merged, no later target changes or new comments on PR111/186 found during research.
Six new/improved candidate streams,681 raw letters; line-split STR/ONG restores continuous8March alignment. Glyph uncertainties preserved.
4February Navy telegram fits COME RETRIBUTION;21February Wirt Adams uses COMPLETE VICTORY; recipient-specific chronology, not general first-use claim.
Located existing OR texts:4February I/49/1p955,8April I/49/2p1216,20April p1255. Additional pointers15January I/45/2p785 and13/14February I/49/1pp978–979; bounded searches did not resolve18January.
20April equipment alignment excludes clear of any;8April manuscript TOWARDS differs from printed TOWARD. Danville segmentation remains uncertain.10February Beauregard still decoded not read.
April10 FX/EVWJ may span a line as one word; trial STORES does not resolve final group. No guessed ending accepted.
No reliable April11 plaintext from known-key trials or hill-climbing Vigenere lengths2–24 using shared en-modern fourgrams; transcription unreliable. No new-key conclusion.
Same112-letter experiment recovers COME RETRIBUTION at0% and5% nominal noise, fails at15%; real optimized outputs rejected as incoherent.
Reproduced all six alignments and source references; raw681/reconstructed682 letters, explicit Danville length mismatch; word shares measured separately.

Follow-up CI required reading_review on four inherited and three new partial texts. Read their supplied prose/alignment; added explicitly labelled model reviews without changing word shares, uncertainty marks or prior attribution. Not independent transcription.
PR205 merged2November; no later target commit or new catalogue681 issue/PR found. Repository-scoped community check.
Completed known-key checks of existing OR15January and13/14February texts. RODDY spelling, date-reference disagreement, finance dating and duplicated boundary words retained.

Three further March13/17 provisional COME RETRIBUTION readings; March8 D.W.Adams COMPLETE VICTORY partial reading aided by existing pencil decipherment. One ten-letter group unread; eleven/ten-letter STEAMBOATS segmentation unresolved.
April11 known-key/convention/global-shift search recovered synthetic controls but no coherent real plaintext. Segmentation errors unmodelled; all real outputs rejected.
Saved six candidate/reconstructed alignments, per-group lengths and lexical measures. Model review only; no independent transcription or complete inventory. See REPORT-2026-11-09.md.

March9 D.W.Adams follow-up adds seventh conditional alignment: COME opening and PRETEXT OF ending. Faint possibly cancelled R before ROAD would restore downstream phase; joined M corrections supported by native crops. Earlier gapped lead preserved.

Maintainer integration of PR #388 (bdpayne): re-ran nov9_analysis.py; it reproduced nov9_alignment.tsv, nov9_controls.txt and the seven per-message cipher/decryption files byte for byte (equal-length agreements 190/213, 221/248, 65/72, 80/87, 68/76, 132/144, 124/135; NOTES' 123/135 for 9 March is superseded by the script's 124/135). nov9_apr11_conventions.py not re-run (en-modern corpus not available offline here).

Brice Dudout: blind transcription of the cipher words of vol. 196 fr. 0030 (to Maury) and fr. 0031-0032 (to D. W. Adams) from the NARA images, frozen by SHA-256 before any key was tried (dudout/blind_transcription_frozen.txt, 10984ebe...); the clear text around each passage was written next to it.

Pre-registered measure (dudout/prereg_fr.md, prereg_measure.py, frozen by hash): mean log10 English letter probability at offset 0 against 200 random 15-letter keys, closed list of five keys. Adams telegram: COMPLETE VICTORY -1.296, rank 1 of 201 (COME RETRIBUTION also rank 1). Maury telegram: FAILED at offset 0 (COME RETRIBUTION rank 10 of 201, -1.572 against a control maximum of -1.517).

Post hoc (found after the test, not pre-registered): the Maury telegram reads with COME RETRIBUTION at offset 0 for its first six words and one place ahead from the seventh (one key letter skipped, or the one-letter word 'a' not copied); with one break and free offsets for every key, COME RETRIBUTION scores -1.271 against -1.463 at most for 200 random keys.

Both telegrams read word by word: 29 of 29 and 44 of 44 cipher words give English that fits the clear text around them; 26 letters in 21 words (Maury 15 letters in 10 words, Adams 11 in 11) needed a one-glyph correction of the kinds already listed for this clerk. The cipher passage of the Adams telegram is not in OR I/49/1 p. 1003 ('* * *').

Integration check by an independent session: the measure, the post hoc check and align.py were re-run and agree with the contributor's files (measure_results.json identical; frozen hashes match); an own decoder from the keys reproduces both decryptions; the NARA images (SHA-256 of fr. 0030 and 0032 as stated) were compared with the transcription: 28 of 29 cipher words of fr. 0030 and 30 of 44 of fr. 0032 viewed, no disagreement.

Source audit by Andrew Beling with AI agents (PR #577, source_audit_2026-11-12/): on the NARA images the 18 January group read QDYXXRQ is ODYXXRO, which gives CONTENT under COMPLETE VICTORY at phase 2, and the 10 April group GJS gives THE under COME RETRIBUTION; both had been proposed from context in PR #186. SENT or TENT on 10 April stays open; three versions of the 11 April ending against the five known keys at every phase (225 comparisons) give no plaintext. No reading or share changed.

Integration check (PR #577) by an AI reader of the project: check.py passes, the two image hashes match on re-download, ODYXXRO and GJS confirmed on the crops. On the 10 April crop two further groups read LYWVEW (SHOUKD for SHOULD) and MF (TO) against the transcription's LVWVEW and NF; recorded in NOTES for the next pass, files not edited.

Follow-up to the PR #577 notes: one AI reader re-read the three disputed groups of 10 April on the full NARA frame 0045, two passes (enlarged grayscale crops; whole line in colour and grayscale) against letter forms on the same telegram. LYWVEW (Y as in XCYKG) and MF (M as in MRU and JMNH) are supported; EIEX leans to E (foot stroke as in EX) and stays open. v11-0045b_transcription.txt updated; decrypts TQOOPS SHOUKD NOT BE SENT TO DEMO POLIS AND PORTIRN OF THE ST ORDS BLTO. No person has checked it; no reading or share changes.

Open frames of entry 681 (vol. 196 fr. 0053, 0056, 0064, 0065, 0071; vol. 11 fr. 0044-0046, 0078-0081; vol. 10 fr. 0056) transcribed twice blind by four AI readers (two per volume), each with a seed telegram first (all passed the 90% mark). Agreement 1230/1317 letters over 12 telegrams; weakest the flowing-capital 11 April telegram on fr. 0046 (60/94). Frames 0078-0081 hold no cipher. blind_2026-11-15/.

Pre-registered test (TEST_PLAN.md, frozen by sha256 before any key was applied): four known keys at all 15 positions on each reader's transcription, quadgram score, one-slip model; 200 shuffles and 200 random keys under the same maximisation; pass above the maximum of all 400. Positive controls pass. 11 of 12 telegrams yield for both readers; the second 11 April telegram on fr. 0046 fails under every key and both models (a miss).

New: 9 March 1865 to Lt Col W. M. Levy (fr. 0056 lower telegram), COMPLETE VICTORY from position 0, 20 of 21 cipher words read, GUAGE needs I for J twice (hole): 155 Mobile and Montgomery cars to be moved on trucks to the wide gauge at Columbus, Ga., under pretense of assisting roads in Georgia. New in part: 11 April 1865 to Maury (fr. 0046 upper telegram), COME RETRIBUTION, 10 of 21 words read, 2 doubtful, 9 unread. Earlier provisional readings of 8, 9, 13, 17 March, 10 April and 18 January confirmed on the blind transcriptions; not applied to their files. Not in profile.outcome.texts and no reading review recorded: left to the reviewers.

Independent verifier (AI) and a second blind helper transcribed the 9 March Levy and the first 11 April telegrams from the images before seeing the work (107/109 and 67/91 letters agreeing), decrypted their own transcriptions with every known key at every position and got the same words; re-ran the frozen test with identical results; classified the letter corrections against the image (GUAGE, OF, TRAINS) and as image-supported alternatives (COLUMBUS, RAIL).

Second 11 April telegram on vol. 11 fr. 0046 (T11, 107 letters), after a frozen plan (blind_2026-11-15/rally_key/key_search/TEST_PLAN.md): known keys used other ways (Beaufort, reversed, restarted, tableau slip), a literature key list and crib dragging all missed; an unconstrained hill-climb over 15-letter Vigenere keys (30 restarts) returned RALLYTOTHEFRONT on reader B1's text (-4.857 against a best of -5.915 on 100 hill-climbed shuffles); on B2's it stopped at GQHAYTOTHEFRONT (11 of 15 letters). Its calibration missed its own mark: 12 of 15 key letters on 5 of 7 known telegrams was required; 3 of 7 for both readers, 5 of 7 for either.

Verification: two further blind transcriptions of T11 by AI helpers told nothing of the key (frozen before decryption): 107 letters, 22 dash-separated groups each; 104 of 107 letters agree, 98-101 with the earlier readers B1 and B2. Both read every one of the clerk's E/F as E, V as Y and the gutter M as D. Both, separately, found faint pencil numerals over cipher letters 30, 45, 60, 75, 90 and 105 (none over 15) and an unclear mark over letter 20.

Frozen verification test (rally_key/verification/TEST_PLAN_verify.md): RALLYTOTHEFRONT on each new helper's first choices, groups giving dictionary words, mark 15 of 22 and 17 of 25 on both, every control below. Miss: 11 of 22 and 12 of 25 on both; controls (400 random English-like keys; the four known keys at all offsets) at most 5 of 22. A second frozen test, a blind classifier on 14 shuffled E/F tiles (this clerk's E has a lower-right tick, his F not), sorted 12 of 14 as the key predicts (mark 12): pass.

New: T11, 11 April 1865, Surget at Meridian to Maury at Mobile (v11-0046b-maury_*), key RALLYTOTHEFRONT from the first cipher letter: 'Let me know EXACTLY HOW LONG YOU WI[L]L HOLD THE CITY as the RUNNING OF THE TRAINS DEPENDS on that. If you can HOLD ON UNTIL NINE O CLOCK TOMORROW Can have four or five ADDITIONAL TRAINS THERE.' All 22 groups give words; one letter is a correction against the image (20, T read, J needed: a hole), ten are image-supported choices, two (the gutter M, a C under a blot) are possible but unsettled. Fits OR I/49/2 pp. 1225-1226 and 1255 (Mobile evacuated on the night of 11 April); not printed there. Not in profile.outcome.texts and no reading review recorded: left to the reviewers.

RALLY TO THE FRONT as a Confederate key or watchword: not in this folder, the repository, OR I/49 pts. 1-2, Friedman's Lecture No. 4 and Introduction to Cryptology IV (keys COMPLETE VICTORY, MANCHESTER BLUFF, COME RETRIBUTION, IN GOD WE TRUST), Plum (1882) vols. 1-2, Bates (1907) or an Internet Archive full-text search. Not opened: Gaddy's chapter in Masked Dispatches (download refused), Kahn's The Codebreakers, Gaddy's Cryptologia articles. The key on every other cipher stream of the folder at all phases: no English.

Integration check of PR #676 (r20). RALLYTOTHEFRONT applied with a separate decoder to the filed letters and to each of the four blind transcriptions of the 11 April lower telegram: against the plaintext given, 1 letter differs on the filed letters (20), 6 on B1, 9 on B2, 12 on helper A, 11 on helper B; 15 places in all, of which five have no reader's first choice (20, 34, 64, 76, 77). NARA frame 0046 fetched again (sha256 d458c966..., as recorded): the six F the key needs lack the tick of the clerk's E; letter 20 is T; letter 77 is not settled; pencil 15s are visible. Own control with the shared English quadgram model: the fixed key on the two later blind transcriptions scores -3.66 and -3.71 per letter, the filed letters -2.25, against -4.10 for the best of 40 shuffles each hill-climbed over all 15-letter keys (median -4.44); an own short hill-climb recovers ...YTOTHEFRONT on B2 and ...TOTHEFRON. on B1. texts.label: 21 Feb 1865, Taylor to Maury: Pensacola, forced reconnaissance, cavalry to the Selma and Montgomery line.
texts.summary: The enemy has left Vicksburg without avowed intention of attacking Mobile; find out what he is doing at Pensacola, by a forced reconnaissance if need be; if no attack from Pensacola is likely, move most of the cavalry on the eastern shore to the Selma and Montgomery line against a movement on Central Alabama.
texts.note: COME RETRIBUTION; 29/29 cipher words, 141/156 letters as read. Fails the pre-registered offset-0 test; one-break check is post hoc (dudout/posthoc_T1_break_results.txt). Integration check: counted in cipher words (29 of 29); 10 of them carry a one-glyph correction, which is counted as read (a correction of the image reading within the clerk's documented confusions, the key being known); counted as holes the share would be 19/29.

texts.label: 21 Feb 1865, Taylor to D. W. Adams: public stores, Cahaba prisoners to Andersonville, Demopolis employees (cipher passage omitted in OR).
texts.summary: Public stores in North Alabama to be put in fortified places or south of the Alabama River; send the Cahaba prisoners to Andersonville on first news of an enemy advance toward Central Alabama; organize the government employees at Demopolis without depriving the workshops.

texts.label: 9 Mar 1865, Bullock for Taylor to Lt. Col. Wm. M. Levy: the Mobile and Montgomery cars to go on trucks to the wide gauge at Columbus, Ga.
texts.summary: Taylor understands there are 155 cars on the Mobile and Montgomery railroad; those not needed daily should go on trucks to the wide gauge at Columbus, Georgia; Levy is to confer confidentially with the superintendent; it might be done under pretense of assisting roads in Georgia.
texts.note: COMPLETE VICTORY from the first cipher letter. Counted in cipher words: 20 of 21; GUAGE is a hole (the image has J twice where I is needed). COLUMBUS takes F where two of four readers read E. v196-0056-levy_read_measure.txt. Decrypted again at integration with a separate decoder: same words.

texts.label: 11 Apr 1865, Surget to Maury: how long Mobile will be held; the running of the trains (key RALLY TO THE FRONT).
texts.summary: Surget asks Maury exactly how long he will hold Mobile, as the running of the trains depends on it; if he can hold on until nine o'clock tomorrow, four or five additional trains can be there.
texts.note: Key RALLYTOTHEFRONT, recovered from the ciphertext alone by hill-climbing (not in any key list opened), standard Vigenere from the first cipher letter. Strict count at integration: 23 words in 22 groups, 21 sure; WILL (letter 20 is T on the image, J needed) and CLOCK (letter 77, read Q by all four readers, C needed) are holes; the contributor counts one hole (22 of 23). The contributor's frozen word test on two new blind transcriptions missed its mark (11 of 22 groups against 15; controls at most 5): recorded as failed. v11-0046b-maury_read_measure.txt.
